2609.05117.title: TIER: Threat Implicitness Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Safety Behaviors
2609.05117.paper_summary: Current LLM safety benchmarks largely rely on binary metrics, overlooking how models respond to harmful prompts with varying threat implicitness. We introduce TIER, a Threat Implicitness Benchmark for behavioral safety evaluation of LLMs. TIER covers four risk domains and four threat levels, from explicit harmful requests to sophisticated jailbreaks. Responses are assessed using a six-label behavior scale and two independent LLM judges. Experiments on six open-weight LLMs show that safety behaviors evolve gradually across threat levels rather than shifting directly from refusal to compliance. Contextual prompts yield the most diverse behaviors, while jailbreaks reveal the largest robustness gaps. Furthermore, models with similar Attack Success Rates can exhibit distinct response distributions, highlighting the need for behavior-aware LLM safety evaluation.
2609.05117.paper_summary_zh: 目前的LLM安全基準主要依賴於二元指標，忽視了模型對不同威脅隱含程度的有害提示的反應。我們介紹了TIER，一個用於LLM行為安全評估的威脅隱含性基準。TIER涵蓋四個風險領域和四個威脅級別，從明確的有害請求到複雜的越獄行為。回應使用六標籤行為量表和兩位獨立的LLM評審進行評估。在六個開放權重的LLM上進行的實驗顯示，安全行為隨著威脅級別的變化而逐漸演變，而不是直接從拒絕轉變為遵從。上下文提示產生了最具多樣性的行為，而越獄行為揭示了最大的穩健性差距。此外，具有相似攻擊成功率的模型可以顯示出不同的回應分佈，突顯了對行為意識的LLM安全評估的需求。
